newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say they restarting war with Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say they restarting war with Kinshasa.

text.p: Zaire rebels said on Sunday they were restarting the civil war against the Kinshasa-based government after a three-day pause and demanded the resignation of President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Rebel leader Laurent Kabila would probably go to South Africa soon to spur negotiations on Mobutu's departure from power, Bizima Karaha, foreign affairs commissioner in the rebel alliance told a news conference in Goma.
"He (Kabila) will go to boost the negotiations, probably to South Africa," Karaha said. It was a "possibility" that Kabila could meet Mobutu face to face, he added.

The rebels fighting to oust Mobutu want a summit between the two leaders before a ceasefire. Last week they declared a "pause" in military operations after the capture of the second city Lubumbashi to give Mobutu time to consider resigning.
"The (appointment of a) new prime minister shows that Mobutu wants violence...Those who say meet violence with violence are right," Karaha said.
"There will never be a ceasefire before negotiations -- never, never, never," Karaha said.
